misroutes.rationale: This is a high-stakes choice among vendor options, and Kepner-Tregoe's must/want criteria weighting and adverse-consequence comparison would test whether the incumbent wins on the merits rather than habit (opportunity-cost and pre-mortem are close alternatives).

A pre-mortem (assume the architecture already failed and reason backward) turns an inarticulate gut feeling into concrete failure paths that can be tested, gated, or mitigated before an expensive, hard-to-reverse commitment.

The decision is made under real uncertainty with no reliable forecast, and effectuation starts from who you are and what you have, caps the downside at an affordable loss, and lets goals emerge from commitments, which fits the identity framing and fear of a wrong call.
